summary: Micafungin is an intravenous echinocandin antifungal that inhibits fungal cell wall beta-1,3-D-glucan synthesis. It is used to treat candidemia, acute disseminated candidiasis, Candida peritonitis and abscesses, and esophageal candidiasis, and for prophylaxis of Candida infections in patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Dosing is by indication and is given as a once-daily 1-hour infusion. No renal dose adjustment is needed, but hepatic effects, hemolysis, hypersensitivity, and infusion reactions require monitoring.
indications: Treatment of candidemia, acute disseminated candidiasis, Candida peritonitis and abscesses
Prophylaxis of Candida infections in patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT)

admin: For intravenous infusion only; infuse over 1 hour
Reconstitute each vial with 5 mL of 0.9% Sodium Chloride or 5% Dextrose (without bacteriostatic agent); swirl gently to avoid foaming - do not shake vigorously
Do not mix or co-infuse with other medications (precipitation can occur)
Inspect for particulate matter and discoloration; do not use if precipitation or foreign matter is present
Slow the infusion rate if an infusion/histamine-mediated reaction occurs
moa: Micafungin is a member of the echinocandin class of antifungal agents. It inhibits the synthesis of beta-1,3-D-glucan, an essential component of the fungal cell wall not present in mammalian cells, leading to osmotic instability and fungal cell death. This gives activity against Candida species.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to micafungin, any component of the product, or other echinocandins
relative: History of hepatic dysfunction (monitor liver tests)

preg: Based on animal findings, micafungin may cause fetal harm. IV administration to pregnant rabbits during organogenesis at four times the recommended human dose produced fetal visceral abnormalities and increased abortion. Human data are insufficient. Advise pregnant women of the potential risk to the fetus; use only if clearly needed.
lact: There are no data on the presence of micafungin in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant or milk production. Micafungin was present in the milk of lactating rats following IV administration. Weigh the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and potential infant risk.
renal: Micafungin does not require dose adjustment in patients with renal impairment, including severe impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min); Cmax and AUC are not significantly altered. It is highly protein bound and not dialyzable. Isolated cases of elevated BUN/creatinine and acute renal failure have been reported - monitor renal function.
hepatic: Liver function test abnormalities have been seen, and isolated cases of significant hepatic impairment, hepatitis, and hepatic failure have been reported, particularly in patients with serious underlying conditions on multiple concomitant drugs. Monitor hepatic function and discontinue if liver function worsens or severe dysfunction occurs.

moderate: Sirolimus (AUC increased ~21% - monitor for sirolimus toxicity; reduce dose if needed)
Nifedipine (AUC +18%, Cmax +42% - monitor for nifedipine toxicity; reduce dose if needed)
Itraconazole (AUC +22%, Cmax +11% - monitor for itraconazole toxicity; reduce dose if needed)
interactions.diagnostics: Elevations in liver function tests, alkaline phosphatase, BUN, and creatinine may occur

serious: Acute intravascular hemolysis, hemolytic anemia, hemoglobinuria

monitoring: Clinical and laboratory evidence of hemolysis / hemolytic anemia
Infusion and injection-site reactions; slow infusion if reaction occurs
counsel: This medicine is given as an intravenous infusion over 1 hour, usually once daily
Report any rash, itching, facial swelling, flushing, or difficulty breathing during or after the infusion
Report dark urine, unusual fatigue, or yellowing of skin/eyes, which may signal hemolysis or liver problems
Tell your team about all other medicines, especially sirolimus, nifedipine, or itraconazole
Complete the full course of therapy as prescribed
pk: Antifungal activity follows IV infusion; ~85% of steady state achieved after three daily doses
Plasma Cmax reached at end of the 1-hour infusion; exposure is dose-proportional
Store unopened vials at 20-25 C (68-77 F); reconstituted and diluted solution at 25 C (77 F); protect from light
pearls: No dose adjustment needed for renal impairment, hemodialysis, or mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment; not dialyzable (highly protein bound)
Few clinically significant drug interactions - mainly modest increases in sirolimus, nifedipine, and itraconazole exposure
Do not co-infuse with other drugs because of precipitation risk
Watch for infusion (histamine-mediated) reactions, hemolysis, and hepatic effects, especially in critically ill patients
missed: Micafungin is administered by a healthcare professional as a scheduled IV infusion. If a dose is missed, give it as soon as possible and resume the once-daily schedule; do not double the dose.
overdose: No cases of overdose have been reported. Repeated daily doses up to 8 mg/kg (max total 896 mg) in adults were given in trials without dose-limiting toxicity. Micafungin is highly protein bound and not dialyzable; manage with supportive care and monitoring.
